name: MindsDB
license: Elastic License 2.0 (source-available, not OSI open source); the integration handlers are MIT

status.note: MindsDB now builds MindsHub, an AI agent workspace, and leaves the query engine to the community; its last release is 26.1.0 (April 23, 2026).

summary: A federated SQL engine that queries over 200 databases, warehouses, apps and files in place, and adds knowledge bases: tables you `INSERT` documents into and `SELECT` from by meaning, for retrieval-augmented generation.
intro: MindsDB, now called the MindsDB Query Engine, is a Python server that puts one SQL dialect over many data sources. `CREATE DATABASE` attaches a source through an integration handler: PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Snowflake, BigQuery, S3, and apps such as Slack, email or calendars. A query planner translates each query, pushes work down to the sources, joins across them and streams the results back, so nothing is copied; you can also send a source its own native query. The server speaks the MySQL and PostgreSQL wire protocols and has an HTTP API with a built-in SQL editor, so `mysql`, `psql`, DBeaver, SQLAlchemy or a BI tool can connect to it like an ordinary database.

Knowledge bases are its semantic layer. A knowledge base combines an embedding model, an optional reranking model and a vector store such as pgvector; `INSERT INTO` a knowledge base chunks, embeds and indexes rows, and `SELECT ... WHERE content = '...'` returns the closest chunks with a relevance score, filtered by metadata columns like any table. Hybrid search runs vector similarity and BM25 keyword matching together, for queries that mix plain language with exact codes. Views save cross-source queries, jobs rerun SQL on a schedule to keep knowledge bases fresh, and agents answer natural-language questions over the attached data using models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Bedrock, Ollama and others.

In 2026 the company renamed its product MindsHub, an agent workspace with a model router and the open-source Anton agent, and its old GitHub repository became MindsHub’s. The engine moved to its own repository, `mindsdb/engine`, as a standalone open-source project that the company says is maintained by the community. Its last release, 26.1.0, came out on April 23, 2026, and later commits are mostly CI housekeeping. mindsdb.com now redirects to mindshub.ai.
strengths: One SQL interface over databases, warehouses, SaaS apps and files, queried live without an ETL pipeline
Retrieval in plain SQL: semantic, keyword and hybrid search with metadata filters, next to joins over live data
Speaks the MySQL and PostgreSQL protocols, so existing clients, ORMs and BI tools connect unchanged
Runs from one Docker image or `pip install mindsdb`
limits: No longer the company’s product: development has largely stopped since April 2026, and support is community-only
Elastic License 2.0, not open source: you can’t offer it to others as a managed service
Federated queries are only as fast as the sources, and joins across sources run in the MindsDB server, so large ones move a lot of data through it
The product changed direction several times, from machine learning in the database to federated queries to agents, so older tutorials often don’t match the current engine

story: Jorge Torres and Adam Carrigan founded MindsDB in Berkeley, California in 2017. Its first open-source release, in 2018, brought basic machine-learning functions into traditional databases, and the name described that architecture. The company went through Y Combinator’s Winter 2020 batch and raised more than $55 million from investors including Benchmark, Mayfield, Y Combinator and NVIDIA.

As large language models arrived, the focus moved from predictions to data access for AI. Between 2023 and 2024 MindsDB added knowledge bases, semantic search and federated queries across documents and other unstructured sources, and it described itself as an engine for AI agents to query enterprise data. In 2025 it launched a separate agents product, and in 2026 it renamed its product MindsHub, keeping MindsDB as the company name. The engine’s last releases, 26.0 in February and 26.1 on April 23, 2026, came from the original repository; the next day its code got a repository of its own, `mindsdb/engine`, and was left to its community.

choices.choice: Speak SQL and existing wire protocols
choices.why: Every analyst and BI tool already speaks SQL and connects to MySQL or PostgreSQL. Presenting models, apps and documents as tables let them use AI features without new client libraries.

Copying data into one store before using it means pipelines to build and data that goes stale. Pushing queries down to each source keeps answers current, at the cost of depending on each source’s speed.

Retrieval for LLMs usually needs a separate vector database and indexing code. Making the embedding, storage and search a table you `INSERT` into and `SELECT` from keeps RAG inside the same SQL as everything else.

timeline.text: Founded in Berkeley by Jorge Torres and Adam Carrigan
First open-source release: machine learning inside the database
Knowledge bases, semantic search and federated queries over unstructured data (2023–2024)
MindsHub Agents launched as a separate product
Product renamed MindsHub; the engine moves to its own repository, last release 26.1.0 (April 23)
